title: Russia sold Alaska for 2 cents an acre, and left a view of tomorrow
description:
In 1867 Russia sold Alaska to the US for $7.2 million, about two cents an acre, and the new border runs between two islands with the date line in the middle. Alaska Day is October 18.

Sources:
- Purchase of Alaska, 1867 (Milestones) — U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian: https://history.state.gov/milestones/1866-1898/alaska-purchase
- Alaska Purchase — Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alaska_Purchase
- Diomede Islands — Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diomede_Islands
- Alaska Economic Trends, December 2018 — Alaska Department of Labor and Workforce Development: https://laborstats.alaska.gov/trends/dec18art2.pdf
- These Two Countries are Separated by 2.4 Miles and 21 Hours — Geography Realm: https://geographyrealm.com/separated-by-2-4-miles-and-21-hours
- Why Did Russia Sell Alaska To The US? — WorldAtlas: https://www.worldatlas.com/articles/why-did-russia-sell-alaska-to-the-us.html

Labels: 'Seward's Folly' was what critics called it; the purchase was approved by the Senate. Big Diomede is 21 hours ahead of Little Diomede in winter (20 in summer).
